In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a product $u(x)\cdot v(x)$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{arsech}⁡x.$

Therefore, we apply the product rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x) \\  & ={(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{arsech}⁡x+\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot {(\operatorname{arsech}⁡x)}^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{x}\cdot \operatorname{arsech}⁡x\,+\,\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{1}{x\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{arsech}⁡x}{x}-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
